sections.h2: Where is Vestavia Hills, and who lives there?
sections.html:
Vestavia Hills is a Birmingham suburb that sits in two counties, Jefferson and Shelby. Wikipedia's city entry, which draws on Census Bureau files, puts the city at 20.352 square miles and says it runs along U.S. Route 31, 7 miles from downtown Birmingham to the north and 4 miles from Hoover to the southwest.

The city is made up of three named areas: Vestavia, Liberty Park and Cahaba Heights. It is the third-largest city in Jefferson County after Birmingham and Hoover, and the fourteenth-largest in Alabama. The city has four ZIP codes: 35216, 35226, 35242 and 35266.

The 2020 census counted 39,102 people in 15,187 households and 15,883 housing units. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 38,306, a drop of 2.0 percent from 2020. A house here is usually sold into a settled, slow-changing community rather than a fast-growing one.

sections.h2: How did Vestavia Hills grow into a city?
sections.html:
Vestavia Hills began as a 1946 subdivision and was incorporated on November 8, 1950. The name comes from Vestavia, the 20-acre estate of former Birmingham mayor George B. Ward on the crest of Shades Mountain. His house, finished in 1925, was modeled on the Temple of Vesta in Rome, and a central portion of the original building remains.

Developer Charles Byrd planned the first subdivision on the southern flank of Shades Mountain for roughly 1,000 people. Growth after that came from new building and from annexation. The decennial counts show how fast it moved:

Houses in a city that tripled in size between 1970 and 2020 come from several building eras. An older house may need work that a newer one does not, and owners often weigh an as-is sale against paying for repairs before listing.

sections.h2: What do the housing numbers say about Vestavia Hills?
sections.html:
Vestavia Hills is mostly owner-occupied and high-income by Alabama standards. The 2010 census recorded a homeownership rate of 76.8 percent, and the 2024 American Community Survey, as summarized on the city's Wikipedia page, lists 13,840 households, a median household income of $134,369 and 15,014 housing units.

Those figures matter to a seller for one practical reason: buyers in a high-income suburb often compare your house with renovated neighbors. A house that needs a roof, kitchen or systems work competes poorly in a retail listing, and a direct cash sale takes that comparison out of the picture.

  • Median household income, 2024 ACS: $134,369
  • Households, 2024 ACS: 13,840
  • Housing units, 2024 ACS: 15,014
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 65.3 percent
  • Median age: 41.7 years

sections.h2: Which county office records a Vestavia Hills deed?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the probate office of the county where the parcel lies, which is either Jefferson County or Shelby County. Check the county on your tax bill before you schedule a closing, because the two offices keep separate records and fee schedules.

Alabama's recordation tax is set by Code of Alabama section 40-22-1. It is 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500. Only the value above any mortgage or vendor's lien that already paid mortgage tax is taxed, and the deed must come with proof of the actual price, on a form the Department of Revenue provides.

The judge of probate calculates the tax when the instrument is presented. Someone who intentionally withholds proof of value after a request pays a penalty of $100 or 25 percent of the tax due, whichever is greater. Deeds written for nominal consideration to perfect title, and corrected deeds, are on the statute's list of exceptions.

sections.h2: When are Vestavia Hills property taxes due?
sections.html:
Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and become delinquent after December 31. The Department of Revenue's property tax FAQ lays out the sequence for unpaid bills: taxes turn delinquent January 1, go to the probate court in February, are advertised in April and can be sold at a May tax sale.

The same page says a county is not required to mail tax notices, so a missing bill is not an excuse. If you sell mid-year, the bill is often still in the previous owner's name, and the buyer answers for the taxes on property they own whatever name appears on the bill. Settle who pays what in writing before closing.

Two reporting rules affect sellers. Owners must sign a new assessment by December 31 to report improvements or removals made on or before October 1, such as additions, pools, decks or a new garage. Re-roofing, minor repairs and painting do not trigger a reassessment.

sections.h2: What about homestead exemptions for Vestavia Hills owners?
sections.html:
A homestead exemption covers a single-family, owner-occupied home and up to 160 acres, claimed for the year in which you live there on the first day of the tax year. The state's FAQ adds that owners over 65, permanently and totally disabled, or blind are exempt from the state portion of the tax, while county taxes can still be due.

You apply at the county office, not with the city. Because Vestavia Hills spans two counties, a homeowner on the Shelby side deals with the Shelby office and one on the Jefferson side with Jefferson's. If you inherited a house and the prior owner held an exemption, ask the office what changes after the transfer.

sections.h2: How do schools, parks and roads shape a Vestavia Hills sale?
sections.html:
Vestavia Hills City Schools is its own district. Per the city's Wikipedia entry it has five elementary schools, two middle schools, one alternative school and one high school, with roughly 6,000 students. Liberty Park Middle School opened in August 2008.

The city runs a parks department with Wald Park, Byrd Park, McCallum Park, the Liberty Park Sports Complex, the Sicard Hollow Athletic Complex and the Cahaba Heights fields. Bus service is run by the Birmingham-Jefferson County Transit Authority as Max Transit. U.S. 31 is the main corridor through the city.

Governance is council-manager. Wikipedia lists Ashley Curry as mayor and Jeff Downes as city manager, which can change after an election, so confirm on the city's own site. Permit rules, rental rules and code enforcement are set by the city, and we did not find them on a page we could confirm, so ask city hall before you assume anything.

sections.h2: What do Vestavia Hills sellers have to sort out before closing?
sections.html:
Most delays come from paperwork rather than from the house. A short checklist keeps a sale on schedule:

  • Confirm whether the parcel is in Jefferson or Shelby County.
  • Pull the latest tax bill and check whether anything is unpaid.
  • Gather proof of the price for the recordation tax form.
  • Report any improvements you made on or before October 1 to the county assessing office.
  • If the owner has died, check whether probate must finish before a deed can be signed.

A cash buyer still goes through the same recording step. What changes is the timeline and the repairs: the buyer takes the house as it stands, and you are not asked to fix the roof, paint or clear the yard. Any written offer depends on the house, the title and the numbers, and we do not promise a price before we have seen them.

faqs.q: Is Vestavia Hills in Jefferson County or Shelby County?
faqs.a: Both. The city lies in Jefferson and Shelby Counties. The county on your tax bill decides which probate office records your deed.

faqs.q: How much is the deed recording tax on a Vestavia Hills sale?
faqs.a: The state privilege tax under Code of Alabama section 40-22-1 is 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed, or fraction of $500, with credit for mortgages that already paid mortgage tax. The probate office also charges a recording fee, so ask the office for its current schedule.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Vestavia Hills?
faqs.a: October 1, and they are delinquent after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue. Unpaid taxes can end up in a May tax sale, so clear any balance before you sell.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Vestavia Hills house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A house does not have to be repaired to be sold, and a cash buyer takes it as is. The deed, tax and title steps are the same as in any sale.

faqs.q: Does the city of Vestavia Hills have special rules for selling a house?
faqs.a: We could not confirm any city-specific seller rule from an official page, so we are not listing one. Call the city's building and code offices to ask about permits and inspections.
